newsitem.title: UK: IPE July Brent closes higher but off day's highs.
newsitem.headline: IPE July Brent closes higher but off day's highs.

text.p: IPE July Brent closed five cents a barrel higher at $20.18 on Thursday, but off the day's new high reached in late trade on the back of a strong NYMEX complex led by gasoline, traders said.

July Brent hit a new high for the day at $20.35 shortly before the close but started slipping in the last 10 minutes as some selling by profit-takers seemed to have set in. "It's just a failure to follow through; on the upside it (July Brent) seemed like it wanted to go higher but it did not really have any momentum and probably just a bit of profit taking finally took us lower on the close". NYMEX's July WTI, whose rise July Brent was following in late trade, closed unchanged at $21.86 but unleaded June gasoline, which was leading the NYMEX complex, closed 0.37 cents up at 66.90 cents a gallon. "Gasoline was the market leader. We were just following the WTI which seems to be following the gasoline," one trader said as July Brent started to climb before the close. Traders said reports of BP cutting refinery runs in Rotterdam by 40 percent would be supportive for products and said they were eyeing a higher open on Friday on gas oil which closed firmer earlier in the day. "The refinery

Traders said on Thursday afternoon that BP, which controls 65 percent of 400,000 bpd Rotterdam Nerefco refinery, had cut runs by the equivalent of 10 percent for the month of May, which translated into a 40 percent cut for the balance of May.
Last week, Texaco cut crude runs at the refinery by the equivalent of 20 percent for the second half of May. But other ARA refiners were holding back from cutting runs on Thursday, traders said.
The recent gains made by the benchmark Brent crude since the start of the month has caused refiners margins in Europe and the Middle East to suffer.
